newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rescuers reach Australian landslide survivor.
newsitem.headline: Rescuers reach Australian landslide survivor.

text.p: Rescuers on Saturday reached a man who survived more than two days buried in the rubble of two Australian ski lodges engulfed by a landslide.

Police said the man was suffering from lacerations and hypothermia. "One of the rescuers managed to put his clenched fist through a small cavity which is 10 cm (four inches) in diameter and has been able to hold hands with the victim," a policewoman told Reuters.
She said rescuers were pumping warm air into the cavity and had managed to feed the survivor warm fluid, a balanced solution of electrolytes and nutrients.

"They managed to pass a small torch (flashlight) through to the man and it has enabled him to describe his present situation to the rescue team," she said. The man, who has not been officially identified, is sandwiched between concrete slabs, three on top and one below.
The slide hit just before midnight on Wednesday at the Thredo resort, 400 km (250 miles) south of Sydney.
Nineteen people were buried in the lodges, while a woman walking home with her husband was swept away with the landslide. Rescuers have confirmed three deaths but only one body has been recovered.
